description: Csikszentmihalyi's finding was that enjoyment does not come from relaxing but from absorption - attention fully occupied, time distorted, self-consciousness gone. Activities with rules and learned skills produce it; passive watching does not.
energy_note: Two hours gone and no memory of them passing.
notes: Flow requires challenge/skill balance, clear goals and immediate feedback.

description: Discovering how much you actually know. Most of the time in the oud is spent on the section that is not working, played or redone until it is. People who stay describe that part as the good part, which is the whole distinction between a hobby and a chore.
energy_note: The repetition is not the price. It is the thing.

description: Even solitary forms improve with one other practitioner in the room. Somebody to show the difficult bar to is worth more than any amount of instruction.
energy_note: One other person who can tell it got better.

description: Equipment, a place to make noise or mess, electricity, and uninterrupted hours - which is where the rest of these datasets attach. Power cuts and shift work end more artistic practice than lack of talent does.
Teaching someone the oud stops being an event and becomes a reference point - retold, compared against, and eventually shorthand inside one family for a whole kind of day.
energy_note: It turns into the story about it.
notes: Experiential purchases retain value through memory where material ones decay; people are markedly unwilling to trade the memory away.
